title: The Quiet Commute
brief: Sample deck: why cities are backing e-bikes.

slides.title: The quiet commute
slides.body: How e-bikes are changing the way cities move
slides.notes: Thanks for having us. In the next ten minutes we'll look at why cities are trading car lanes for bike lanes, what riders get out of it, and what a pilot would look like.

slides.title: What we'll cover
slides.notes: Four parts: the shift we're seeing, what riders tell us, the cost comparison, and a simple path to a pilot.

slides.title: Cities are trading car lanes for bike lanes
bullets: Protected lanes make short trips feel safe
Electric assist flattens hills and distance
slides.notes: The change is structural, not a trend: safer infrastructure, better bikes, and employers looking to cut commute emissions all point the same way.

slides.title: Riders show up when the lanes do
slides.body: Usage climbed fastest on routes where protected lanes opened first.
slides.notes: In Paris, e-bike trips more than tripled after the city built out protected lanes. Placeholder figure for the sample deck.

slides.title: Trips grow every year the network does
slides.body: Sample data: daily e-bike trips on a city network, thousands.
slides.notes: Each year the network grows, daily trips follow. Sample data only.

slides.title: An e-bike costs a fraction of a car
slides.notes: Annual running cost of a car versus an e-bike, sample figures.

slides.title: A pilot in three steps

steps.title: Map
steps.text: Pick two corridors with protected lanes and dense employers.

steps.title: Equip
steps.text: Place a small fleet with charging at partner sites.

steps.title: Measure
steps.text: Track trips, retention and rider feedback for one quarter.

slides.notes: We keep it small and measurable: map, equip, measure. One quarter is enough to see retention.

quote.text: I get to work calmer than I ever did in the car, and I'm never late.
quote.name: Sample rider

slides.notes: This is the kind of feedback pilots generate. Sample quote for the template.

slides.title: Three reasons riders stay

cards.title: Faster than traffic
cards.text: Door-to-door times hold steady at rush hour.

cards.title: Cheaper than a car
cards.text: Running costs are a small fraction of driving.

cards.title: No parking to find
cards.text: Ride to the door, lock up, walk in.

slides.notes: Speed, cost and convenience, in riders' own order of importance.

slides.title: Start a one-quarter pilot
slides.body: Two corridors, one fleet, clear numbers at the end.
slides.notes: Our ask: a one-quarter pilot on two corridors. We'll share the measurement plan this week.
